column1: # Swipe accuracy of a whole build, from its SHIPPED files (dictionary, sentence pack, swipe model). One row per measurement.
# set: bench-2000 / test-extra-10000 = real English swipes (public MIT test split, never trained or tuned on);
#   '-futo-scorable' = only the swipes FUTO's scorer counts (target of 2+ letters, more than 2 trace points);
#   heliboard-LANG = real HeliBoard Gesture Data swipes (CC BY-SA, test only, no sentences, per-swipe real key boxes).
# context: yes = the previous words of the sentence are given; no = none (with a sentence pack: scored as a sentence's first word).
# sentence_pack: yes = the build's LANG.ngram ranks the guesses; no = dictionary word frequency only.
# Rows dated before 2026-10-24 are earlier measurements copied from docs/active/specs/2026-10-23-own-swipe-engine.md,
#   bench/history.tsv and bench/languages/ (not re-run); an empty cell = not recorded.
# match: letters = lower case, letters only (don't = dont); lookup = lower case, accents kept, apostrophes/hyphens dropped.
# notes "junk" = share of shown alternatives (guesses 2-3) that are stretched ("youuuuu"), rare (word-list frequency
#   under 80 of 255) or rarely used names (capitalised, under 120); "alternatives useful" = when the first guess is
#   wrong, how often the right word is among the alternatives. Both printed by tools/swipekb-bench.
